title: Diagnose release-specific application 500 and roll back safely
trigger: A customer-facing API route begins returning HTTP 5xx after a release while infrastructure/dependency health may remain green.
preconditions: confirm the affected customer route and reproduce the failure through the public path
capture the failing release version and X-Request-ID
check readiness plus PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, and proxy health before changing them
verify customer/business data exists when the symptom could be mistaken for data loss
correlate the failing request into the application layer using logs and traces
identify an approved known-good release before rollback
diagnostic_steps: compare /health/ready with the failing customer transaction
verify the affected ticket row directly in PostgreSQL when applicable
search Nginx and API logs using the same edge-owned request ID
confirm centralized Loki evidence for the request
confirm Tempo trace evidence for the request
determine whether the 5xx originates in Nginx, application code, or a dependency before remediation
mitigation_steps: do not restart or reconfigure healthy PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, or Nginx without evidence
do not hot-edit application code on the running container
when a release-specific application defect is proven and an approved known-good release exists, roll back the application release
retain the bad version, request ID, logs/traces, reproduction, and rollback evidence for development
validation_steps: re-test the exact customer request that failed before rollback
run the complete customer/release verification after rollback
confirm readiness and dependency health remain healthy
attach an L3 escalation package for permanent code correction when the defect is application-owned
escalation_boundary: Escalate to development/L3 when the failing request is proven to reach application code and the defect requires a code change. Escalate to incident command/platform when rollback is unsafe, the known-good release is unavailable, multiple layers fail simultaneously, data integrity is uncertain, or the customer impact exceeds the normal L2 rollback authority.
